doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

title: Jazz audiences in England and Japan; Ted Heath
summary: Jazz is better appreciated overseas, American players move to Europe, and Joe sang on a Ted Heath radio show that impressed her father.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Can you give me an idea of what the English audience was like for jazz music when you first were going back and forth.

Very enthusiastic. Very enthusiastic, and also in Japan, very enthusiastic. In fact, the jazz artists who have been there say they’re better known in these other countries than in the United States. And I remember in Japan a man coming up to Joe with a whole album of things about Hank Jones that we were talking about, he had Hank’s whole history, all his records, he had all Joe’s stuff, he had all Sweets’ stuff. And this is a man in Japanese, a gentleman in Japan. And you know that would be rare here I think. They are much more appreciated overseas.
In Japan and Europe, Switzerland, Germany, all these places.
Yes, which is why so many escape to France and Paris and Johnny Griffin lives in France and some others in Denmark.
Isn’t Ernie Wilkins, I think he’s—
I don’t know if Ernie Wilkins — is Ernie still with us?
I thought so, the musician’s union had a Denmark address.
His brother Jimmy lives in Las Vegas. Jimmy Wilkins. He has a band.
And the musicians in England would pick up on American styles, mostly from record I would imagine.
The great band when I was living there was Ted Heath.
Ted Health, yeah. They still play his great recordings.

Yes. And Joe did a wonderful radio show with Ted Heath in which he sang “Old Man River” at breakneck speed, which was a tremendous success, yes. My father, who had never heard Joe sing at that point, listened to it, and he said “that was Joe, my God he can really sing.” So it was all very impressive. That was great.
